name: Tech, data & hackathons
blurb: Model-building competitions, research paper tracks, and sponsored hackathons. The strongest category for work an AI coding agent can help produce.

name: Forecasting & prediction
blurb: Probability tournaments scored on accuracy. Free to enter, cash pools published per tournament, and most of the work is research and calibration.

name: Sports & fantasy picks
blurb: Free-to-play pick'em and fantasy games from media and league operators. Low effort per week, but the field is large and payouts are concentrated at the top.

name: Creative & photography
blurb: Judged writing and photography prizes. Free entry exists, but eligibility and submission windows are strict and prizes are often part equipment.

name: Trivia & quizzes
blurb: Knowledge games that advertise cash. Most models pay in points or crowdfunding position rather than a fixed operator prize pool.

name: Skill tournaments
blurb: Mobile skill games. Free rooms typically pay gems, not dollars; real cash usually sits behind an entry fee. Check before spending time.

name: Market simulations
blurb: Paper-trading and market-prediction contests. Lead-only in this pass: every entry still needs an official rules check.

name: Pool software
blurb: Tools for running office pools. The money is contributed by your group, not paid by the operator, so these are not cash-prize competitions.

name: Directories
blurb: Lists and aggregators that help you find events. Useful for discovery, but they are not competitions and cannot verify a prize.
